name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Adopt the 2px #005fcc focus ring with a 1px #fff inset at 70% opacity. This keeps the ring visible on all backgrounds while reducing visual noise, which matters for users with cognitive or vestibular sensitivities. The trade-off is a slightly softer ring that may blend more on high-contrast displays, but the inset ensures clarity without harsh edges.

name: Reader
text: The 2px #005fcc ring with 1px #fff inset at 70% opacity risks failing WCAG 2.2 AA on light backgrounds where the white inset disappears, leaving only a faint blue ring. A safer alternative is a 3px solid #005fcc ring with a 1px #fff outer stroke—it meets contrast on all backgrounds and is easier to see for users with low vision. Test both options with a screen reader and high-contrast mode to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt the 3px solid #005fcc focus ring with a 1px #fff outer stroke at 70% opacity. This guarantees WCAG 2.2 AA compliance on every background while keeping the ring crisp and unmistakable for keyboard users. The trade-off is a slightly bolder ring that may feel heavier in dense UIs, but that’s a usability win outweighing minimal visual noise.

name: Reader
text: The 3px solid #005fcc ring with a 1px #fff outer stroke risks looking like a border on dense interactive elements, which could confuse users. A better alternative is to use a slightly thicker ring, like 4px, with a subtle animation to differentiate it from a static border. This would settle the argument if we can test it with real users and confirm that the animated ring is distinguishable and usable for everyone, including those with visual or cognitive impairments.
